senses.gloss:
Saurapurāṇa
(‘the purāṇa concerning सूर्य or the Sun-god’)
------------------------------------------
The पुराणस् are the secondary sources of Hindu religion and culture. They are broadly classified into two divisions: The mahāpurāṇas and the उपपुराणस्.
Though tradition counts them as 18 in each group, the उपपुराणस् as they are listed now are at least 29.
They were taught by सूर्य or आदित्य to मनु, his own son.
The Saurapurāṇa is one of them. It has 3900 verses spread over 69 chapters. It belongs to the Śaiva group of पुराणस्. Its contents, which are variegated, may be summarised briefly as follows:
Greatness of शिव and the effect of devotion to him as also his मन्त्र (Oṁ namaśśivāya); construction of शिव temples, worship of शिव as also several stotras or hymns to him.
Several stories like the destruction of दक्ष’s sacrifice, शिव’s मर्रिअगे to पार्वती, birth of स्कन्द (Subrahmaṇya), killing of तारकासुर, destruction of Tripuras or the three cities of the demons, उपमन्यु being blessed with an ocean of milk and विष्णु getting his सुदर्शन discus by the grace of शिव.
On places of पिल्ग्रिमगे like काशी, उज्जयिनी, the river गङ्गा and several other places.
Prāyaścittas (expiations), śrāddhas (obsequial rites), varṇāśramadharmas, details of च्रेअतिओन् as also some sādhanas according to योग.
Thus, this purāṇa can be considered an important work on शैविस्म्.
